newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai parties to meet as army, elders urge calm.
newsitem.headline: Thai parties to meet as army, elders urge calm.

text.p: Leaders of Thailand's six coalition parties were due to meet on Wednesday to discuss who would replace besieged Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa as the army chief and an elder statesman urged reconciliation.

Army Commander General Pramon Phalasin and Prem Tinsulanonda, former prime minister and current Privy Councillor, made separate statements urging politicians to put aside their personal differences for the good of the country.

"The Privy Councillor said he is concerned about the current political situation and he wished to see the coalition partners seek a resolution," foreign minister Amnuay Viravan told reporters when asked what he discussed in a meeting with Prem.

"He told us to set aside the emotional and personal and individual conflicts because the immediate problem is causing damage to the country. He said we should find a way to resolve the problem as soon as possible," Amnuay said.
Banharn announced on Saturday he would step down from his post in seven days, after finding a suitable successor.

But he is currently in a standoff with his coalition partners over who would replace him. Coalition allies agreed to back Banharn in a no-confidence vote in parliament on Saturday only if he agreed to quit.
Rumours have been swirling around Bangkok since Saturday over who might be named premier as parties jostled for power to win support for their candidates.
Defence Minister and New Aspiration Party leader, General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, is one of the front-runners tipped to be named prime minister.
Top Chart Thai advisor Pramarn Adireksarn, 82, has also claimed he had a right to the top post because he was a senior Chart Thai leader and had party support.
Former premier and leader of the opposition Chart Pattana Party, Chatichai Choonhavan, may be chosen as a compromise choice, politicians and analysts said.
The battered Thai bourse, which has tumbled in recent months over political uncertainly, was also volatile as various rumours emerged about who might be named to Thailand's top job.

On Tuesday the SET index rebounded in afternoon trade on rumours in the market that Chatichai might become the new prime minister, rising 7.84 points to 1,042.21. In early trade on Wednesday the index was down to 1,031.42 points at 0350 GMT.
Army Commander Pramon urged control and asked politicans to think of the people instead of desiring power.
He said the military, which has led 17 attempted or successful coups since parliamentary democracy was set up in 1932, had no plans to get involved in politics.
"I do not wish to see the military getting involved in politics and vice versa," he said.
But he said the present coalition partners should carefully consider how to overcome current problems, as anything done without careful consideration of public opinion could be doomed to failure.
Some analysts and politicians have speculated if the coalition could not agree on a new leader, Banharn could dissolve parliament and call snap elections.
